adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — updateManyByCredentialId(id, {}) with empty data may be a no-op in Prisma, so SelectedCalendar.updatedAt never bumps and the "refresh" silently passes.
matched_golden_ids: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe that calling updateManyByCredentialId with an empty data object results in no actual update, so Prisma's @updatedAt field (SelectedCalendar.updatedAt) does not get bumped during a refresh, leading to incorrect/undetected cache refresh status.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — The bump runs for every SelectedCalendar under the credential, including ones this call never refetched, so stale calendars get marked fresh.

adjudication.rationale: In `CalendarService.ts`, the new line `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` (commented as updating `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` for all calendars under the credential) clearly applies to *all* `SelectedCalendar` rows with that `credentialId` (see `updateManyByCredentialId` implementation: `where: { credentialId }`). The finding’s concern about this being broader than the specific calendars refetched is grounded in the diff, but whether this is actually incorrect (i.e., that `updatedAt` is used as a per-calendar “freshness” signal and thus becomes misleading) is not directly verifiable from the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:29 — deleteCache wipes the CalendarCache rows but leaves the SelectedCalendar googleChannelId watch in place, so the watch cron will not re-subscribe and the cache stays empty until Google happens to push a change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteCache.handler.ts` only deletes `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` and does not touch `SelectedCalendar`/`googleChannelId`. However, the claim that leaving `googleChannelId` causes “the watch cron will not re-subscribe” and “cache stays empty until Google pushes a change” depends on cron/subscription logic that is not present in this diff. From the diff alone, we cannot verify that deleting cache should also clear/refresh watches or that failing to do so breaks behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:69 — "Delete cached data" is offered for delegation credentials, but deleteCacheHandler only accepts credentials with userId === user.id, so the action always errors for those users.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, the cache actions are shown whenever `hasCache` is true (`isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`) and are not gated by `delegationCredentialId` (only disconnect is: `canDisconnect = !delegationCredentialId && ...`). However, `deleteCacheHandler` only allows deleting cache for a credential where `id` and `userId: user.id`. For delegation credentials (indicated by a non-null `delegationCredentialId` passed through from `SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper`), the UI can still offer “Delete cached data” but the backend may reject it with "Credential not found or access denied", causing an error for those users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:26 — Throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, so an unauthorized or missing credential comes back as a 500.
matched_golden_ids: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out that throwing a generic/plain Error in tRPC (especially for auth/unauthorized cases) results in an incorrect 500 response, and that the handler should instead throw a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code (e.g., FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND) to reflect the real error type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28 — The connectedCalendars handler creates CalendarCacheRepository directly, skipping the feature-flag/mock path, so cache status is queried and shown even when calendar-cache is disabled.

adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, the code now does `import { CalendarCacheRepository } ...` and `const cacheRepository = new CalendarCacheRepository();` before calling `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(...)`. The diff also introduces an `ICalendarCacheRepository` interface and a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` explicitly meant to be used when calendar-cache is disabled (it logs “Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled”). By directly instantiating the concrete `CalendarCacheRepository` in the handler, this change hardcodes the DB-backed implementation and makes it harder/impossible for any existing feature-flag/DI mechanism (if present elsewhere) to swap in the mock/disabled implementation in this path. However, the diff alone does not prove that a feature-flag/mock selection mechanism exists or that cache will definitely be shown when disabled; it only shows the direct construction.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:43 — The deleteCache mutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars (only the optional onSuccess callback does), so the UI can keep showing a stale "last updated" status after a delete.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess?.()`; unlike `disconnectMutation`, it does not call `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()` (or otherwise update cached query data). This means the UI refresh after deleting cache is dependent on the parent-provided `onSuccess` callback doing a refetch/invalidate, which is not guaranteed by this component itself. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded issue, though whether it manifests as stale UI in this PR depends on how `onSuccess` is implemented at call sites (not shown here).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:25 — New deleteCache mutation throws a plain Error for missing/unowned credential, surfacing as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a typed TRPCError (NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN) for clients.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the handler checks ownership via `prisma.credential.findFirst(...)` and on failure does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. With the mutation defined directly in the TRPC router and no error translation shown in the diff, this will propagate as an untyped exception (commonly `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`) rather than a structured `TRPCError` (e.g., `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`) that clients can reliably handle.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28 — connectedCalendars response shape now depends on a directly instantiated CalendarCacheRepository, bypassing the CalendarCache.init feature-flag/mock path so cacheUpdatedAt is exposed and queried even when calendar-cache is disabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` now directly imports and instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` and always calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, then always returns `cacheUpdatedAt` in the response (`enrichedConnectedCalendars`). That does bypass any potential repository-selection/feature-flag mechanism suggested by the existence of `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` (which logs “due to calendar-cache being disabled”). However, the diff does not show the actual `CalendarCache.init`/feature-flag wiring, so it’s not provably a runtime defect—more of an architectural/feature-flag consistency concern introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:69 — Delete-cache action is offered for delegation credentials, but deleteCache contract only accepts credentials with userId=ctx.user.id, so delegation-credential callers always get an error.

adjudication.rationale: In CredentialActionsDropdown, the cache actions are shown whenever `isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` (`hasCache`), regardless of `delegationCredentialId` (only disconnect is gated by `canDisconnect = !delegationCredentialId && ...`). However, `deleteCache.handler.ts` authorizes by `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })`, so a delegation credential (not owned by `ctx.user.id`, as implied by existing comments that delegation credentials can’t be disconnected) will fail with "Credential not found or access denied" when attempting delete-cache. This is broken behavior introduced by the diff (UI offers an action that backend rejects for delegation creds).

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts:21 — Exported UserWithCalendars type now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on selected calendars, breaking any external caller (e.g. platform API v2) that builds the user with the old narrower select.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts`, the exported `UserWithCalendars` type was changed so `allSelectedCalendars` and `userLevelSelectedCalendars` items are now `Pick<SelectedCalendar, ... | "updatedAt" | "googleChannelId">[]` instead of the prior narrower pick. That is a type-level API tightening: any code constructing a value typed as `UserWithCalendars` (e.g., via Prisma `select` that omits these fields) would no longer type-check. The diff shows at least one internal select was updated (`UserRepository` now selects `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId`), but the claim about breaking “external caller (platform API v2)” is not directly verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — updateManyByCredentialId is called with empty data `{}` to bump updatedAt; Prisma may short-circuit or not set @updatedAt on empty updates, so the "touch" can silently do nothing

adjudication.rationale: In `CalendarService.ts` the new call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` is explicitly intended to “Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt”, but it passes an empty `data` object. The repository forwards this directly to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`. With no fields to update, Prisma will either reject the call (empty update) or perform a no-op; in either case it won’t reliably “touch” rows to bump an `@updatedAt` column. This means the added logic can silently fail to update `updatedAt` as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:26 — Throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError(NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN), so an authorization failure shows up as a 500 internal server error

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `deleteCache.handler.ts`, an auth/access failure (`if (!credential)`) is handled by `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In a tRPC mutation this will typically be surfaced as an `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (500) rather than a semantically correct `TRPCError` with `FORBIDDEN`/`NOT_FOUND`, so the finding is directly grounded in the diff and indicates incorrect error behavior for an authorization failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27 — Instantiates the real CalendarCacheRepository unconditionally, skipping the feature-flag/mock selection, so cache status still gets queried and shown when calendar-cache is disabled

adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` the new code imports and instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly and always calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(...)`. The diff also shows a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` whose methods explicitly log “Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled”, implying there is (or should be) a mechanism to select mock vs real when the feature is disabled. This handler bypasses any such selection/injection by hard-coding the real repository, which at minimum defeats the “no-op when disabled” intent (extra DB query), and could surface cache status if rows exist. The diff alone doesn’t show the feature-flag selection mechanism, so the impact is architectural/behavioral but not fully provable as a hard defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:35 — Looks up cache status by credentialId, but delegation-credential calendars use in-memory credentialIds while cache rows are keyed to real credentials or userId, so cacheUpdatedAt is always null for them

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` collecting `credentialIds` directly from `connectedCalendars` and looking up `CalendarCache` rows by `credentialId` via `groupBy` (new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`). Nothing in this diff indicates that delegation credentials use “in-memory credentialIds” different from the persisted `Credential.id`, nor that cache rows are keyed to “real credentials or userId” instead of `credentialId` (the schema/migration explicitly adds `CalendarCache.updatedAt` and keeps `credentialId Int` as the key). The claim about delegation calendars therefore isn’t verifiable from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:9 — Backfilling updatedAt with NOW() makes every existing CalendarCache row look freshly synced, so the new cache-status UI shows a misleading "last updated" time for stale legacy caches.

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds `updatedAt TIMESTAMP(3) NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` to existing `CalendarCache` rows, and the schema sets `updatedAt @default(now()) @updatedAt`. The new cache-status UI pulls `updatedAt` via `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` which returns `_max.updatedAt` per credential and the UI displays it as “Last updated”. For preexisting cache rows, `DEFAULT NOW()` will populate `updatedAt` with the migration time, making stale legacy cache entries appear recently updated in the UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:1 — Unrelated local-dev Tunnelmole script (mutates ../.env, macOS-only sed) is bundled into a calendar-cache feature PR.
apps/web/package.json:11 — Unrelated dev:cron change from ts-node to npx tsx is a stray tooling bump outside the PR scope.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a tooling/script change in `apps/web/package.json` where `dev:cron` switches from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`. The rest of the PR is focused on calendar cache/status UI, TRPC routes, repositories, and Prisma schema/migrations. This package.json script change appears orthogonal to those functional changes, so it is a concrete “unrelated change in the same PR” scope concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:28 — Handler deletes calendarCache rows via raw prisma, bypassing the CalendarCacheRepository/ICalendarCacheRepository abstraction the PR extends elsewhere.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the handler calls `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` directly instead of going through the `ICalendarCacheRepository`/`CalendarCacheRepository` abstraction that this PR is extending and using elsewhere (e.g., `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` and calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`). This is a concrete architectural consistency/testability concern introduced by the change, but not a verifiable correctness/security defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28 — Directly instantiates concrete CalendarCacheRepository instead of the feature-flag-aware path, making the newly added mock implementation effectively dead.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` importing and instantiating `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly, but it does not show any existing “feature-flag-aware” factory/selection path that should have been used instead, nor does it show how/where `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` is intended to be wired in. The claim that the mock is therefore “effectively dead” (and that this bypasses a feature flag) cannot be verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts:899 — updatedAt and googleChannelId are added to the selectedCalendars select and UserWithCalendars type but are never consumed by this change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` to both the `UserWithCalendars` type in `packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts` and to the `selectedCalendars` select in `packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts`, but no code in this diff reads those fields (the new UI uses `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache`, not `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, and `googleChannelId` is not referenced). This appears to be unnecessary data fetching/type widening within the scope of this change, though it does not introduce a direct functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — updateManyByCredentialId(id, {}) relies on an empty-data update implicitly bumping @updatedAt, an obscure side-effect coupling with no explicit field set.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` in `CalendarService.ts`, and the repository method directly calls `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`. With `data: {}`, this change appears intended solely to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` via Prisma's `@updatedAt` behavior (and/or whatever DB defaults exist), but no explicit field is set, creating a non-obvious coupling/side-effect dependency. The finding is grounded in the diff; whether Prisma permits/executes an empty update and bumps timestamps cannot be verified from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:53 — Re-implements the credentials.delete mutation, toasts, invalidations and confirm dialog already encapsulated in DisconnectIntegration, duplicating logic.

adjudication.rationale: The new `CredentialActionsDropdown` does inline the disconnect flow (calls `trpc.viewer.credentials.delete.useMutation`, shows success/error toasts, invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `utils.viewer.apps.integrations`, and wraps it in a `ConfirmationDialogContent`). The wrapper was changed to use this new component instead of `DisconnectIntegration`, so this change plausibly re-creates logic that could have been reused to avoid divergence. However, the diff does not show `DisconnectIntegration`’s implementation, so the claim that it already encapsulates the exact same behavior isn’t fully verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — Every webhook-triggered cache refresh now issues an extra updateMany touching all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential (write amplification/row churn on a hot path) just to bump updatedAt, which the UI does not even read (it uses CalendarCache.updatedAt).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` in `CalendarService.ts` (with a comment indicating it’s to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`), which would run on each cache refresh and potentially update many rows for the credential (write amplification on a hot path). In contrast, the newly added UI cache indicator is fed by `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, which derives `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` via `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, not from `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. The performance/row-churn concern is therefore diff-grounded, even if the necessity of the SelectedCalendar bump isn’t evidenced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — updateManyByCredentialId with empty data `{}` may be a Prisma no-op that never bumps @updatedAt, and a failure here throws out of fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache after the cache was already written, failing the webhook/cron run

adjudication.rationale: In `CalendarService.ts` the new call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is intended (per the adjacent comment) to bump `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, but the diff shows it passes an empty `data` object to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany`. With no fields to update, this is at best a no-op that won’t change `updatedAt` (so the intended behavior isn’t achieved), and it may also throw at runtime depending on Prisma’s validation. The call is not wrapped in error handling, so a throw would occur after `setAvailabilityInCache(...)`, potentially failing the overall cron/webhook execution despite having written cache.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:29 — Cache-status lookup is unguarded and bypasses the calendar-cache feature flag, so any calendarCache query error fails the entire connectedCalendars query instead of degrading to null status

adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, the new logic unconditionally instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` and calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(...)` with no feature-flag/DI indirection or try/catch. The diff also shows a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` whose methods explicitly log "Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled", implying there is a disabled mode that should avoid DB access. This handler bypasses that and will propagate any prisma/groupBy error, failing the entire `connectedCalendars` response instead of degrading `cacheUpdatedAt` to null.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:25 — Throws plain Error instead of TRPCError NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN, surfacing as a 500 and triggering client error handling/retry semantics for an expected auth miss

adjudication_records.issue_text: scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh:17 — cleanup always exits 0, so rate-limit and URL-extraction failures report success to callers; ENV_FILE "../.env" is cwd-relative and reused-tunnel URL comes from a possibly stale/missing log

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh, the cleanup() function unconditionally does `exit 0`, and it is invoked on error paths (rate limit hit and failed URL extraction both call `cleanup`). This makes the script report success (exit code 0) even when it explicitly prints failure messages. Additionally, the “tmole already running” branch reuses a URL by grepping LOG_FILE (/tmp/tmole.log) without ensuring it exists or is current for that running tmole process, so it can produce an empty/stale TUNNEL_URL and still exit 0 via cleanup on failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:1024 — updateManyByCredentialId(id, {}) relies on Prisma bumping @updatedAt when data is empty, and no test checks that updatedAt actually changes, so this could silently do nothing.
